newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aurora says Indonesia gold reserves rise.
newsitem.headline: Aurora says Indonesia gold reserves rise.

text.p: Aurora Gold Ltd said on Thursday that exploration success at its Mt Muro project in Indonesia's Kalimantan province had lifted proven and probable reserves by 208,000 ounces to a total of 1.346 million ounces.

Aurora managing director Ian Burston told Reuters that the increase was based on a rise in probable reserves to 304,000 ounces from 96,000 ounces gold equivalent at the Batu Tembak-Bantian lode system.
Burston said Mt Muro continued to produce highly encouraging results at areas of known mineralisation and new targets, highlighting the potential for further reserve upgrades.

The Mt Muro mine maintained low cash costs of US$201 per ounce for the March 1997 quarter, with production at 54,022 ounces gold equivalent, representing 40,707 ounces of gold and 934,178 ounces of silver.
This performance was slightly down on the December 1996 result but steady with the previous March quarter and in line with budgets for the year, the company said.

At the company's other major Indonesian target, the Toka Tindung project, Aurora said mining consultants Snowden Associates had estimated a total indicated and inferred resource of 8.93 million tonnes grading 2.35 grams per tonne gold and
4.63 g/t silver, containing 675,000 ounces of gold.
Clough Engineering Ltd had been appointed to carry out a feasibility study at Toka Tindung, which Aurora said it planned to develop as its second major gold operation in Indonesia.
